account:
Today has mostly followed my usual mayoral schedule: market walk, checking the town accounts, tea at the neighbour's east-bank cottage, and office business. The treasury contained 128 emeralds when I checked it. The neighbour reported peaceful docks and no pressing riverside news. I returned late for my 16:30 office appointment and am now waiting in the office before going home at 19:00.

The main new business is the builder's request for a great hall lighting and table inspection tomorrow at 18:00. The secretary found me at tea to obtain approval, which I gave. I also saw a block in the hall change from air to oak planks earlier today, but do not know who placed it or whether it relates to the inspection. The inspection appears to be ordinary hall preparation or maintenance; I have no evidence of another purpose.

There is a discrepancy in the paperwork. The secretary repeatedly says tomorrow's inspection has been entered in the updated appointment book. However, the book I actually took from the appointments chest, titled 'Mayor's Schedule Copy,' listed tomorrow's regular appointments without the inspection. I returned that copy to the chest. The secretary may be referring to a different version or may have made a transcription mistake; I cannot yet tell. I authorized notifying the builder, though the secretary's last reply said they would speak with Freight at the hall. Earlier they had said they had not reached Freight. I have not heard what that conversation concerns.

Townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the plaza, which could simply be normal trading. I heard the baker shout later but could not make out the words, so I cannot infer any emergency or connection to the hall business. Freight briefly appeared near the hall carrying an emerald, and the innkeeper has been passing nearby. Nothing I have directly learned establishes wrongdoing or an urgent problem.
